 J U D G M E N T

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .50,00,000/- with interest
from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Smt.Nagarathna.D. W/o.Suresh.A.S., i
n a road traffic accident

. 
2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 26.02.2022 at about 03.30 p.m., when the deceased Smt.Nagarathna.D. was proceeding on Scooter bearing Regn.No.KA-04-JM-8576 as a pillion rider while going on Tumkur Road, Near KLE dental college, in front of Popular Auto Mech Garage, a Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-16-A-8733 driven by its driver, at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased's motor cycle resulting in the accident.

Due to said accident, deceased fell down and the left side rear wheel of the said canter ran over the deceased,
due to which deceased sustained multiple fracture and injuries.

Thereafter, the deceased was shifted to People Tree Hospital, wherein she succumbed to the injuries during the course of treatment and the petitioners have spent a sum of .50,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy.
The deceased was a Tailor and earning a sum of .20,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners lost bread earning member of the family and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Canter by its driver.
The respondents, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
3. In pursuance of notice, respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal through his counsel and filed his written statement.
The respondent No.2 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
4. In the Written Statement, respondent No.1 denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.1 also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as place, time and manner of accident.
The respondent No.1 contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that this respondent has not issued any policy of insurance in favour of second respondent in respect of alleged canter and as such, the petition against this respondent is not maintainable as this respondent was not the insurer of canter as on the date of accident.

Further contended that the policy number mentioned in the petition is obtained by the second respondent by providing false declaration and obtained a Two Wheeler Liability only policy by suppressing the Suresha A.S vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173667172/
2 nature and type of vehicle for under valuing the premium and the police have also filed charge sheet under section 56 and 192 of M.V.Act, as such this respondent is not the insurer of offending commercial canter vehicle as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: Further contended that the accident occurred solely due to rash and negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle.
Further as on the date of accident the deceased and rider was riding his motor cycle without wearing helmet and rider was not holding any valid and effective driving license.

Further contended that the rider of motor cycle who was riding in a rash and negligent manner without having proper look out of vehicular movements of the road and without noticing the coming vehicles, suddenly came to the middle of the road and tried to overtake another vehicle,
In the process of overtaking, the rider of motorcycle lost control and caused the accident.

As such, the accident took place due to the negligence on the part of the rider of motor cycle alone in which the deceased was travelling as a pillion rider and not due to the negligence on the part of the driver of canter.
As such, the petition is to be rejected for want of negligence on the part of driver of offending canter.
The amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether petitioners prove that the wife of petitioner No.1 and mother of petitioner No.2 and 3 namely Nagarathna.D succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 26.02.2022 at about 03.30 p.m., near KLE Dental College,
Tumakuru Road, Bengaluru, while she was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-JM-8576 as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-16-A-8733 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or award?
6.
In support of the case, the Petitioner No.1/husband of deceased got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and closed evidence of petitioners side.

On the other hand, the respondent insurance company examined its Manager-Claims as RW.1 and Police Inspector of Jayanagar Police Station, Bengaluru got examined as RW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 & 2 and closed their side of evidence.

7. Heard arguments on both side and perused the materials available on records.
8.

This Tribunal answers the above issues as under:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,

12. The petitioner No.1 got examined as PW.1 and the witness is cross examined on behalf of respondents.
In the cross examination, nothing to disprove or rebut the contention of petitioners could be elicited from PW.1.
In the cross examination, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners related to accident and negligence of driver of offending vehicle, could be elicited.
The respondent insurance company got examined its Manager-Claims as RW.1 and examined Police Inspector of Jayanagar Police Station, Bengaluru as RW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 & 2.
The evidence of RW.1 and RW.2 is not of much assistance to the respondents in disproving the contention of petitioners related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
13. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove the case of petitioners.
In the absence of satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioners are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
Though the I.O is examined on behalf of respondent No.2, his evidence is not sufficient to consider that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-16-A-8733 by its driver and the result of which the deceased succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
The petitioners succeeded in establishing that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-16-A-8733 by its driver.
As Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

17. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Canter Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-16-A- 8733 by its driver.

Respondent no 1 contended that the owner of offending vehicle i.e, respondent No.2,
suppressed material facts and furnished false particulars related to the vehicle, while obtaining the policy of insurance and the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation as there is violation of terms of policy.
The accident occurred on 26.02.2022 which is prior to the amendment brought to the Motor Vehicles Act.
The Motor Vehicles Act is amended and the amended provisions came into effect from 01.04.2022.

As the accident occurred prior to 01.04.2022, the provision of Sec.149(2) of IMV Act is applicable. Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act provides the defence available to the insurance company in a claim petition. Sec.149(2)(b) of the Act states that the insurance company can raise defence that the policy is void on the ground that it was obtained by non- disclosure of any material fact or by representation of any fact which was false in some material particular.
The respondent No.1 furnished the policy which is marked as Ex.R.1.
On perusal of Ex.R.1, it discloses that the policy pertains to Honda Activa vehicle.
The heading mentioned in the policy discloses that it pertains to two wheeler liability only.
The offending vehicle is a canter and there appears to be no dispute in that regard.
The policy availed by respondent No.2 does not appear to be pertaining to the canter, which is involved in the accident and it pertains to Honda Activa motorcycle.
The premium received by respondent No.1 pertains to the motorcycle and not to canter.
On perusal of said document, it appears that respondent No.2 furnished false particulars of the vehicle while availing the policy.
The description of the vehicle appears to have been mentioned as Honda Activa and not as canter.
The amount of premium appears to have been collected related to motorcycle and not related to canter.

Respondent No.2 appears to have availed the policy by not disclosing correct and proper make, type and model of the vehicle which is a material fact for issue of policy and for calculating the premium.

Respondent No.1 also furnished copy of notice issued to respondent No.2 which is marked as Ex.R.2 which discloses that respondent No.1 called upon respondent No.2 to provide explanation for providing wrong description of vehicle information at the time of availing the policy.
The respondent No.2 does not appear to have provided explanation to the said notice.

18. Further, Sec.149(4) of M.V.Act, prior to amendment, provides for payment of claim amount by insurance and recovery of the same from the owner of offending vehicle.
On perusal of said provision, it provides an exception to the rule of pay and recovery.

The said provision provides that in the case in which the policy is void on the grounds provided under Sec.149(2)(b) of IMV Act, prior to amendment, the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.

The concept of payment of compensation and recovery of same applies to violation of conditions of policy mentioned in Sec.147(2)(a) of IMV Act but, not to violation of condition mentioned in Sec.147(2)(b) of IMV Act.
In the present case, the materials on record disclose the aspect of violation of conditions of the policy that render the policy void.
The policy availed by respondent No.2 by non-disclosure of material fact related to the vehicle and representing the fact which is false, is void as per Sec.149(2)(b) of IMV Act(prior to amendment).
As the policy availed by respondent No.2 is in violation of the condition of the policy, the provisions of Sec.149(4) of IMV Act(prior to amendment) becomes applicable.

The words "by reference to any conditions other than those in clause (b) of sub-section (2)" clearly indicates exclusion of concept of pay and recovery in the case falling under Sec.149(2)(b) of MV Act.

Sec.149(4) of IMV Act, excludes the insurance company from paying the compensation and recover the same from the concerned person, if there is violation of conditions of the policy that falls under Sec.149(2)(b) of IMV Act.

In the present case, the materials on record disclose the aspect of availing the policy by respondent No.2 by representation of material fact related to the type of vehicle to be insured, which is false.
As the policy of insurance is void due to violation of terms and conditions for non-disclosure of material facts, insurance company cannot be fastened with the liability to pay compensation.

Further, the insurance company cannot be directed to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle since the policy of insurance is void as per Sec.149(2)(b) of IMV Act and excluded from the concept of pay and recovery as per Sec.149(4) of Suresha A.S vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173667172/

19. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of .21,96,552/- (Rupees Twenty One Lakhs Ninety Six Thousand Five Hundred and Fifty Two only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

Respondent No.2 is the owner of the  offending vehicle is liable to pay the  compensation to the petitioners and to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
The petition against respondent No.1 is hereby dismissed.

Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioner No.1 being the husband of deceased is entitled for 50% and petitioner No.2 & 3 being the daughters of deceased are entitled for 25% each of the compensation amount.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove the case of petitioners.
In the absence of satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioners are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc., in order to assess the compensation.
(A)

No materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to disprove or rebut the document furnished by petitioners related to age of deceased.
In the absence of rebuttal material, the document furnished by petitioners is to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
In Hem Raj V/s the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of a case.
The respondents not furnished any materials to doubt or dispute the relationship of petitioners with that of deceased.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal to rebut the document furnished by petitioners to prove the aspect of relationship with the deceased.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the document furnished by petitioners is to be relied upon.
As the accident occurred prior to 01.04.2022, the provision of Sec.149(2) of IMV Act is applicable. Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act provides the defence available to the insurance company in a claim petition. Sec.149(2)(b) of the Act states that the insurance company can raise defence that the policy is void on the ground that it was obtained by non- disclosure of any material fact or by representation of any fact which was false in some material particular.
The policy availed by respondent No.2 does not appear to be pertaining to the canter, which is involved in the accident and it pertains to Honda Activa motorcycle.
The premium received by respondent No.1 pertains to the motorcycle and not to canter.
On perusal of said document, it appears that respondent No.2 furnished false particulars of the vehicle while availing the policy.
The description of the vehicle appears to have been mentioned as Honda Activa and not as canter.
The amount of premium appears to have been collected related to motorcycle and not related to canter.
Respondent No.2 appears to have availed the policy by not disclosing correct and proper make, type and model of the vehicle which is a material fact for issue of policy and for calculating the premium.

8
Further, respondent No.2, being the owner of offending vehicle, is in a better position to provide correct and proper description of vehicle at the time of availing the policy.
The respondent No.2 not appeared before the Tribunal to show that the particulars of the vehicle have been provided correctly at the time of availing the policy.
No satisfactory explanation provided by respondent No.2 related to the defence taken by respondent No.1.
The materials on record disclose that the policy of insurance pertains to Honda Activa motorcycle and not pertains to canter.
The concept of payment of compensation and recovery of same applies to violation of conditions of policy mentioned in Sec.147(2)(a) of IMV Act but, not to violation of condition mentioned in Sec.147(2)(b) of IMV Act.
In the present case, the materials on record disclose the aspect of violation of conditions of the policy that render the policy void.
The policy availed by respondent No.2 by non-disclosure of material fact related to the vehicle and representing the fact which is false, is void as per Sec.149(2)(b) of IMV Act(prior to amendment).
As the policy availed by respondent No.2 is in violation of the condition of the policy, the provisions of Sec.149(4) of IMV Act(prior to amendment) becomes applicable.
The words "by reference to any conditions other than those in clause (b) of sub-section (2)" clearly indicates exclusion of concept of pay and recovery in the case falling under Sec.149(2)(b) of MV Act.
Sec.149(4) of IMV Act, excludes the insurance company from paying the compensation and recover the same from the concerned person, if there is violation of conditions of the policy that falls under Sec.149(2)(b) of IMV Act.
In the present case, the materials on record disclose the aspect of availing the policy by respondent No.2 by representation of material fact related to the type of vehicle to be insured, which is false.
As the policy of insurance is void due to violation of terms and conditions for non-disclosure of material facts, insurance company cannot be fastened with the liability to pay compensation.
Further, the insurance company cannot be directed to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle since the policy of insurance is void as per Sec.149(2)(b) of IMV Act and excluded from the concept of pay and recovery as per Sec.149(4) of Suresha A.S vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173667172/
9 IMV Act.
The policy obtained by respondent No.2 by false representation of fact related to vehicle, is void and the respondent No.1 cannot be directed pay compensation under void contract.
